messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Hi all BioGeoBEARS users,

I've refactored some code and moved some functions etc. so there are some new files to source; the full list is below (also in the PhyloWiki script).  Let me know if issues remain after sourcing the full list.

I have added some new features, I will do an official announcement at some point (hopefully I can get this all on CRAN soon). The ones that might be most interesting to play with:

1. A new parameter, "w", which is an exponent on the manual dispersal multipliers matrix (so you can test whether your manual dispersal multipliers might be a better explanation if taken to some power, rather than just being forced to fix your manual dispersal multipliers to your best guesses.  w=1 (default) means the manual dispersal multipliers are used unchanged (as normal). w=0 would mean the manual dispersal multipliers are all rescaled to 1, etc.  This doesn't solve all issues with manual dispersal multipliers but may help reduce subjectivity there.

2. A new parameter, "n", which is an exponent on an "environmental distances matrix". This works identically to the regular distances matrix and x exponent; but having the second matrix lets you add a second sort of distance between areas, e.g. environmental distance or whatever you like. I am dubious about how often you will be able to get statistical support for this (with 3-10 areas, there aren't that many different distances on which to fit these parameters), but it can be tried at least.

3. I've added an area adjacency matrix file option, which should work like the one in python Lagrange. It works just like areas_allowed, by removing states that don't match, but the interpretive code is different than areas_allowed, so that it matches the Lagrange likelihoods.  This should work for both normal and stratified analyses. Note that, with this method, you cannot e.g. exclude ABD but keep ABCD in the state space. If you want to do such a thing (can you justify allowing ABCD but disallowing ABD?), you could do it by manually modifying the states_list (or lists_of_states_lists_0based for stratified runs) and storing these in the BioGeoBEARS run object. As usual, you have to ensure that your state space allows the included states to be connected so that your data has a likelihood greater than 0 (ln likelihood greater than -Inf).

4. The stratum boundaries are now plotted on time-stratified output plots by default.

Let me know if issues arise. Cheers!

Nick

===============

messages.subject: BioGeoBEARS validation tests, including Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping (BSM)
messages.subject_clean: BioGeoBEARS validation tests, including Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping (BSM)
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Short version: I have posted a bunch of validation examples to: http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-validation, and gotten stochastic mapping to be consistent with ancestral state probabilities. Everyone should source the new validated code, whether or not they are doing stochastic mapping at the moment. The source() commands are near the top of the example script: http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

Long version: It took some serious digging in the code, but I have finally figured out what the issue was with the preliminary stochastic mapping code that I created last year. My expectation was that if one did many stochastic maps under the ML model and took the average, this should equal the ancestral state probabilities calculated analytically under the ML model.  The problem was that this was only roughly true in my earlier tests -- state probabilities, especially those with the highest-uncertainty (probabilities between 0.25 and 0.75) tended to correlate with the analytic probabilities less than expected.

There were several subtle issues I had to fix including a default fixed value for a random number seed (I was changing the seed progressively in an early experiment, but it was too easy to forget), details of using the uppass calculation, and try statements to catch errors when the simulation step is attempting to simulate a valid history on a branch.

As part of figuring this out I set up a number of validation examples to test ancestral state probabilities between normal and stratified BioGeoBEARS, between them and Liam Revell's phytools (for a case where BioGeoBEARS can implement the phytools unordered character model). I haven't tried comparison to diversitree stochastic mapping but I did show the ClaSSE model can be reduced to equal the various BioGeoBEARS models.

The validation is posted here:

Biogeobears Validation
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-validation

Basically, everything now lines up well compared in several different ways, and this is good evidence that both the ancestral state probabilities and the BSM are working correctly, in both the non-stratified and stratified versions.

I won't claim it's perfect (post issues to the Google Group as always), but I'm happy enough with it to add the updates to the source() commands at the beginning of the script. As usual, after every library(BioGeoBEARS) command, source the revised code:

================
library(BioGeoBEARS)
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_add_fossils_randomly_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_basics_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_calc_transition_matrices_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_classes_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_detection_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_DNA_cladogenesis_sim_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_extract_Qmat_COOmat_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_generics_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_models_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_on_multiple_trees_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_plots_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_readwrite_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_simulate_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_SSEsim_makePlots_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_SSEsim_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_stochastic_mapping_v.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_stratified_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/BioGeoBEARS_univ_model_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/calc_uppass_probs_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/calc_loglike_sp_v01.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/get_stratified_subbranch_top_downpass_likelihoods_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/runBSM_v1.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/stochastic_map_given_inputs.R")
source("http://phylo.wdfiles.com/local--files/biogeobears/summarize_BSM_tables_v1.R")
calc_loglike_sp = compiler::cmpfun(calc_loglike_sp_prebyte)    # crucial to fix bug in uppass calculations
calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch = compiler::cmpfun(calc_independent_likelihoods_on_each_branch_prebyte)
    # slight speedup hopefully
================

Yes, this source() thing is getting ridiculous, but it's only until I get a new CRAN version up. An alternative that takes up less space in your script is to download all of these files to some directory and use the BioGeoBEARS sourceall() command to source all of the .R files in that directory.

The best example code for stochastic mapping at the moment is "Psychotria_M0_unconstrained_BSMs.zip", at:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-validation#BGB_nonstrat_DEC_DECj

You will have to make your own modifications to source the code above, set your working directory, etc. I eventually hope to have a tutorial etc. that runs automatically on defaults, but that will take awhile.

Cheers,
Nick

messages.body_plain:
> > Hi Nicholas: I have been working through your example scripts for DEC and DEC+J with a couple of my own files and have successfully gotten to the point where I can visualize ancestral states (states or pie graphs) and compare models. Is there an easy way to get probabilities for different ancestral areas in tabular format along the lines of Lagrange output? The tree I am working with has 252 terminals and it would be convenient to have the output in tabular format so that I can track down various nodes of interest. Thanks in advance. Sincerely, Mark Springer
Here's the  answer:

1. Probabilites of states/ranges at each node:

####################################
# Probabilites of states/ranges at each node
####################################
# What you want, if "res" is your results object, is:

res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node

# In this table:
# - columns are states/ranges
# - rows are nodes, in APE order (tips, then root, then internal)

#  You can see the node numbers and  same APE order with:
prt(tr)

# You can plot APE node labels with:
plot(tr)
axisPhylo()
nodelabels()
tiplabels(1:length(tr$tip.label))

More hints here:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#working

names(res) will show you other information in the results object

Some other things:

2. Be careful interpreting ancestral range probabilities, see:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#Most_prob_states_not_joint

3. Note that I did major updates and validation checks (http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-validation ) on the code recently, so you should make sure you source() all the revised .R files, as shown near the beginning of the updated example script:

http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#script

(if you were using this already, you should be fine)

Cheers!
Nick
